messages:
mina: quick thread to resolve packaging/upgrade ownership after the airgap rfc review. main question: should the operator ever re-sign artifacts or only assert activation via ephemeral receipts?

allen: leaning toward operator-as-verifier only. re-signing gives the operator too much power and hides provenance from admins.

ria: operator doing heavy fetches before activation was our pain point on small nodes. we should avoid full materialization unless strictly required.

oliver: suggestion: packaging pipeline emits sealed bundle = {manifest.json (signed), chunk-index.bin, blob-refs}. operator validates signature and writes an activation-record; it does not alter bundle signatures.

mina: +1. activation-record should be minimal: manifest_id, node_id, activation_ts, operator_ephemeral_sig, nonce. no signing of bundle content by operator.

janet: for airgapped restores admins must be able to run an offline verifier that checks manifest.signature and the activation-record chain. so the verifier needs to trust operator ephemeral certs only if those certs chain to an operator root that admin trusts.

allen: operationally we also need a seeded installer mode: admin can prefetch specific chunk ranges to disk before bringing operator up. That avoids duplicate downloads and keeps disk churn low.

ria: to support seeded installs the chunk-index must include byte ranges and expected digests so an installer can place partial files in the right offsets. operator should resume streaming/validation and skip re-downloading chunks that match digests.

deploy-bot: bundle published: id=sha256:ac9b..., manifest=manifest-2026-03-21T09:00Z

oliver: GC/rollback complexity: if a node cleaned old blobs, and we need to roll back, operator must either fetch from local mirror or error with clear recovery steps. we need tombstone policy metadata on the manifest to indicate fallbacks.

mina: propose policy fields: retention_days, allow_remote_reseed (bool), mirror_hint (URL or mirror-id). default retention_days = 7 but operator config can increase.

janet: security: prevent replay of activation-records. include manifest_epoch and nonce. record operator certificate serial in audit log. ephemeral keys must rotate and rotation events be auditable.

allen: cli idea: `rwctl verify --manifest manifest.json --activation activation.json` prints PASS/FAIL and a short bullet list: missing-blobs, invalid-signature, expired-activation, stale-ephemeral-cert. Minimal UX for onprem admins.

ria: edge case: partial activation across a fleet. some nodes may have activated and GC'd others not. operator should expose rollout state and ability to orchestrate rollback only when majority of nodes can satisfy blob availability or kick off reseed jobs to mirrors.

oliver: implementation note: operator RBAC change: remove any long-lived signing keys and restrict to ephemeral signing of activation receipts only; packaging service holds bundle signing keys.

mina: action items: 1) add chunk-index byte-range spec to packaging RFC, 2) define activation-record schema and anti-replay rules, 3) update operator RBAC doc to remove signing privilege, 4) draft `rwctl verify` CLI output strings. i'll draft a follow-up rfc with these sections.

janet: i'll draft the CLI error strings and sample audit events.

allen: i'll sketch the seeded-installer layout and seeding tooling expectations.

mina: thanks — this keeps operator responsibilities small, preserves auditable provenance, and gives admins the tools they need for airgapped restores :+1:
